title: Model actors in the CLI and MCP

claims.text: culture-rules enrols each local model as its own actor from the gateways' /v1/models, lists where an actor is used, repoints a workflow from one actor to another and refuses to disable an actor still in use: one CLI verb and one MCP tool each, dry-run by default

honesty_conditions.text: culture-rules learn and the MCP tool list both show actors enrol-models, actors references and workflows repoint-actor, and actors disable carries the reference guard

claims.text: actors enrol-models reads each gateway's /v1/models; it takes more than one gateway URL, so the lobes gateway or a machine's own gateway can serve as the source (operator, 2026-10-19)
A model actor's concurrency pool defaults to the model name; an override maps a model to an existing pool, e.g. cortex-spark2=qwen-spark2 (operator approved, 2026-10-19)
One actor per local model lane (cortex-spark, cortex-spark2), never a task-named actor; the step stays work-agnostic and its configuration specialises it (operator, 2026-10-19)
Repeated script runs against the store belong in the CLI and MCP, like rollouts (operator, 2026-10-19)
The operator and the assisting agent who run culture-rules from the CLI or MCP and wire local models into workflows

honesty_conditions.text: The verbs are documented where the operator looks: explain catalog, learn, and docs/operations (a model-actors section)

claims.text: Pointing a workflow step at a local model means hand-building actor JSON, editing the workflow JSON with its revision, and disabling the old actor: a multi-step script in the scratchpad (model-actors.sh, 2026-10-19), and actors update even needs a positional ID that the operator's first command missed

honesty_conditions.text: The scratchpad script model-actors.sh needed build/create/point/retire/check steps and hand-built JSON for one repoint (2026-10-19)

claims.text: Three verb calls replace the script: actors enrol-models makes or updates one agent actor per matching model, workflows repoint-actor moves a workflow's steps to it with expected_revision, and actors disable refuses while an enabled workflow still names the actor; actors references shows where an actor is used

honesty_conditions.text: An end-to-end test against MemoryStore: enrol two models from a fake /v1/models, repoint a workflow, then actors disable on the old actor succeeds only after the repoint

claims.text: Every lobes lane (cortex-spark, cortex-spark2, worker-thor, hand-spark2) becomes a ready actor any workflow can use, and moving work between lanes is a reviewed dry run instead of hand-edited JSON

honesty_conditions.text: One enrol-models run against the live lobes gateway with --match 'cortex-*' plans exactly cortex-spark and cortex-spark2, and nothing else

claims.text: actors enrol-models takes repeatable --gateway MACHINE=URL and --api-key grant:NAME (default grant:LOBES_GATEWAY_API_KEY); the server resolves the grant reference to GET URL/v1/models, as GET /actors/{id}/discord/targets does for the bot token, and the actor stores params.api_key as the grant reference, never the value

honesty_conditions.text: A test asserts the bearer key comes only from the named environment variable, never appears in output, --json or the stored actor, and the stored params.api_key is grant:<name>

hard_questions.text: The URL serves two readers, the CLI host listing models and the actor's machine calling the model: is one URL enough (e.g. spark's actor on its LAN address 100.127.105.72:8001), or does each gateway take a separate stored base_url (e.g. the loopback 127.0.0.1:8001 the newspaper actor uses today)?
hard_questions.resolution: (a) one URL per gateway, read by the server and called from the actor's machine; spark=http://127.0.0.1:8001 as today, a machine gateway on its LAN address (operator, 2026-10-19)

revisions.text: actors enrol-models takes repeatable --gateway MACHINE=URL; it GETs URL/v1/models with a bearer key read from an environment variable named by --api-key-env (default LOBES_GATEWAY_API_KEY, injected with grant run --inject), and the actor stores the key as params.api_key grant:<name>, never the value
revisions.reason: server-side reading (c17 amended): the key no longer has to be on the CLI host

claims.text: actors enrol-models enrols only models matching a repeatable --match glob (no default, so embedders, rerankers and Hugging Face names like unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 are never enrolled by accident); the actor id is the model id, and a model id that is not a valid actor id is refused

honesty_conditions.text: A test feeding the live model list (cortex-*, embedder-*, reranker-*, unsloth/...) plans only the --match hits, and a match with no valid id is refused with exit 1

claims.text: Each enrolled actor is kind agent, on the gateway's MACHINE, with params base_url = URL, model = the model id, concurrency_pool from c3, max_concurrency 1; an existing actor with that id is updated only in those fields, a matching one is unchanged, and the plan shows create/update/unchanged per actor

honesty_conditions.text: Running enrol-models twice in a row plans 0 changes the second time; an actor edited by hand keeps every field outside the enrolled ones

hard_questions.text: The lobes gateways on spark and spark2 list the same lanes (both serve cortex-spark and cortex-spark2): when two --gateway entries serve one model, which gateway and machine does its actor get - the first --gateway listed, a refusal unless --prefer names one, or one actor per gateway with a suffixed id?
hard_questions.resolution: (a) the first --gateway listed wins; other gateways serving the model show as 'also served by'. No second actor for the same model: refused when defined and checked at runtime (operator, 2026-10-19)

claims.text: actors references ID lists every workflow step (loop bodies included) whose action params.actor is ID, and every rule whose action names it, with workflow, step and enabled state; read-only

honesty_conditions.text: A test with a step inside a for_each body and a rule action naming the actor lists both

claims.text: workflows repoint-actor WORKFLOW --from A --to B rewrites every params.actor == A in the workflow, loop bodies included, and PUTs with expected_revision; it refuses when B is missing, disabled or deleted, or when no step names A; it never edits description or notes, and lists steps whose notes mention A as warnings

honesty_conditions.text: Tests: a stale revision returns the 409 revision_conflict as a CliError; description and notes are byte-identical after a repoint; missing or disabled --to refuses with exit 1

claims.text: actors disable ID refuses, in the dry run too, while an enabled workflow or rule still references the actor, naming them; --force disables anyway

honesty_conditions.text: A test: disable is refused while an enabled workflow references the actor, allowed once it is repointed, allowed with --force; a disabled workflow does not block

claims.text: Each new verb follows the CLI contract (dry run by default, --apply, --json, exit 0/1/2, CliError, explain catalog entry and learn mention) as a thin wrapper over its endpoint; MCP gets each as a tool through the registry, and the parity test covers them

honesty_conditions.text: tests/test_mcp_parity (or its equivalent) passes with the new verbs, and uv run teken cli doctor . --strict stays green

revisions.text: Each new verb follows the CLI contract: dry run by default, --apply commits, --json, exit 0/1/2, CliError, an explain catalog entry and a learn mention; MCP gets each as a tool through the registry, and the parity test covers them

claims.text: The logic lives in the server, so the CLI, MCP and site share one implementation: POST /actors/enrol-models (dry_run plan, then apply), GET /actors/{id}/references, POST /workflows/{id}/repoint-actor (dry_run, expected_revision), and POST /actors/{id}/disable refusing 409 actor_in_use unless force; api/openapi.json pins them, and a server + node rollout ships them

honesty_conditions.text: git diff main shows no change under culture_rules/server or api/openapi.json
tests/server/test_openapi_contract.py passes with the four endpoints pinned in api/openapi.json, and the web client's types compile against them

revisions.text: No API or api/openapi.json change and no new server endpoint: the verbs compose existing API calls on the client, like actors enrol-agents (culture_rules/cli/_commands/actors.py), so no node or server rollout is needed
revisions.reason: operator 2026-10-19: the site gets the feature too, as part of the Actors page; server-side logic avoids a TypeScript copy of the Python planner

claims.text: llm.complete's locked brief stays as it is; moving the brief into step config is the separate newsletter work (review table row 1)
No automatic disabling or deletion of actors whose model has left a gateway; enrol-models only creates and updates, and reports models it no longer sees

The committed newspaper bundle (docs/rules/newspaper) moves its summary step to cortex-spark2 and drops actors/newspaper-llm.json for a cortex-spark2 actor; docs/operations/newspaper.md and the bundle tests follow

honesty_conditions.text: tests/rules/test_newspaper_bundle.py and test_newspaper_flow.py pass with the bundle on cortex-spark2, and grep finds no newspaper-llm under docs/rules

claims.text: On the live store, 3 commands with no hand-written JSON (enrol-models, repoint-actor daily-newspaper, actors disable newspaper-llm) leave daily-newspaper's 1 llm.complete step on cortex-spark2, and the next 05:00 issue has 4 of 4 section summaries written by cortex-spark2

honesty_conditions.text: The 3 live commands are recorded with their output, and the next issue's run record shows the summary step's actor as cortex-spark2 with 4 summaries

claims.text: The Actors page gains: an 'Add models from a gateway' panel (gateways, match, pool overrides; shows the server's plan, then applies), a 'Used by' list on an actor (from references, linking each workflow), a 'Move to another actor' action on that list (repoint, with the revision-conflict Reload), and Disable showing the in-use refusal with the workflows named

honesty_conditions.text: vitest and Playwright cover the panel's plan-then-apply, the Used by list, a repoint with a stale revision showing Reload, and the refused Disable; the webglass agent-state gate stays green
Screenshots of the Add models panel, the Used by list, the Move action and the refused Disable, in light and dark, are sent to the operator and approved before merge

hard_questions.text: The design canvas is the editor's visual source of truth: is the Actors-page shape (a panel plus a Used by list on the actor) fine to build from the existing Actors board style, or should it get a canvas design first?
hard_questions.resolution: Build the panel and the Used by list in the existing Actors board style; screenshots go to the operator for review instead of a canvas design first (operator, 2026-10-19)

claims.text: No change to the engine or to any action kind, except one added refusal in llm.complete (model_taken, c26); the new endpoints only read and write actors and workflows through the store

honesty_conditions.text: git diff main shows no change under culture_rules/node, culture_rules/engine or culture_rules/model/action_kinds.py
git diff main under culture_rules/node and culture_rules/engine shows only the model_taken check in node/actions/llm.py and its tests

revisions.text: No change to the node daemon, the engine or any action kind: llm.complete runs exactly as today, and the new endpoints only read and write actors and workflows through the store
revisions.reason: q1 decision: the one-model-one-actor rule is also checked at runtime

claims.text: q1: the first --gateway listed wins; no second actor may hold the same model, tested at definition and at runtime (operator, 2026-10-19)
q2: one URL per gateway serves both the server's /v1/models read and the actor's calls (operator, 2026-10-19)

One enabled actor per model: creating or updating an enabled agent actor, or enabling one, whose params.model is already held by another enabled agent actor is refused (409 model_taken, naming the holder and saying to disable it first) in POST/PUT /actors, POST /actors/{id}/enable and enrol-models' plan; a disabled actor holds nothing; at runtime llm.complete refuses a step whose actor's model is also held by another enabled actor (model_taken)

honesty_conditions.text: Tests: a second actor with model cortex-spark2 is refused on create, on update and in the enrol plan; a store seeded with two such actors makes llm.complete fail with model_taken; the live newspaper-llm/cortex-spark2 pair is resolved by the rollout order (repoint, then disable) before the check bites

Tests: create, update and enable of a second enabled actor for cortex-spark2 each return 409 model_taken naming the holder; the same actor created disabled is allowed and enables once the holder is disabled; enrol-models plans the refusal; a store seeded with two enabled holders makes llm.complete fail with model_taken

hard_questions.text: Today newspaper-llm already holds cortex-spark2, so enrolling cortex-spark2 would hit the new check: should enrol-models take over (rename) an existing actor holding the model, or must the operator repoint and disable newspaper-llm first?
hard_questions.resolution: (a) only an enabled actor holds a model; enabling a second actor for a model already held is refused with an error naming the holder; the one-time move is actors disable newspaper-llm --force, enrol-models, repoint-actor (operator, 2026-10-19)

revisions.text: One actor per model: creating or updating an agent actor whose params.model is already held by another non-deleted agent actor is refused (409 model_taken naming the holder) in POST/PUT /actors and in enrol-models' plan; at runtime, llm.complete refuses a step whose actor's model is also held by another enabled actor (model_taken), so a duplicate that predates the check or was written to the store directly never runs
revisions.reason: q4 decision (a): only enabled actors hold a model, and enable is checked too

claims.text: q3: the Actors page additions follow the existing Actors board style, reviewed from screenshots, no canvas design first (operator, 2026-10-19)
q4: only an enabled agent actor holds its model; enabling a second actor for the same model is refused with an error naming the holder (operator, 2026-10-19)

scope_entries.finding: Both gateways list the same lanes plus embedders, rerankers and HF names (cortex-spark, cortex-spark2, worker-thor, hand-spark2, embedder-*, reranker-*, unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4), so enrolment needs a match filter and a collision rule
enrol-agents is the precedent: GET /actors, plan_enrolment diffs desired vs existing into create/update/disable changes, applies through POST/PUT only with --apply
One MCP tool per registry verb (noun_verb, params_schema), so new CLI verbs become MCP tools with no extra code
actors update and disable take a positional ID; workflows update sends expected_revision (_REVISIONED); disable has no reference guard today
The one llm.complete reference is at summarise.body[summary].config.action.params.actor = newspaper-llm; the summarise step's notes name newspaper-llm
llm.complete needs an agent actor whose params carry base_url and model; the call runs on the actor's machine, so base_url must be reachable from there
Today's actor stores base_url http://127.0.0.1:8001 (spark loopback), api_key grant:LOBES_GATEWAY_API_KEY, pool qwen-spark2, machine spark
The Actors page edits one actor at a time (ActorForm, AppConfigForm for app surfaces, CommandsEditor); it has no bulk-add, no references view and no repoint today

The server already resolves a grant: reference per request (secrets.resolve, injectable resolve_secret for tests) to call an external service for an actor: the precedent for reading /v1/models server-side
Rollouts have server endpoints (/rollouts*) but no site page, so the rollout precedent covers CLI+MCP over endpoints; the site page is new ground
